raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Split MRV2 CUDA graph descriptor generation into decode-only and prefill/mixed builders. `_init_candidates()` retains the shared sorting and candidate indexing. Fixes #61881.

## Claims

Preserves the shared capture sizes, descriptor order and dispatch priorities. Adds regression tests for mode/LoRA selection and rounded-size deduplication.

## Validation

Baseline: `957d512e96`. H100, BF16, MRV2; both checkouts use the same native build.

- 87 tests passed on the updated branch, including 16 added cases; pre-commit passed.
- 960 configurations / 76,800 dispatch comparisons: identical capture plans, candidate lists and decisions.
- Composition with #56136 (`6ab4d6a43f`): reproduced the missing-import failure before the follow-up; both merge orders now produce the same conflict-free file, and all 46 combined planner/dynamic-SD tests pass.
- Follow-up Qwen3-4B/DFlash MRV2 smoke: 41 requests, dynamic K=5/3/1, FULL target/drafter replay, and nonzero acceptance.
- Qwen3 engine A/B: matching capture plans and actual FULL graph replay in every configuration below; nonzero speculative acceptance.

| Target / drafter | TP | Speculation |
|---|---:|---|
| Qwen3-8B | 1 | Disabled |
| Qwen3-8B / Qwen3-0.6B | 1 | K=3 |
| Qwen3-4B / DFlash | 1, 2 | Dynamic K=5/3/1 |
| Qwen3-4B / DSpark | 1 | Adaptive verification |

The full TP=1 workloads cover 128/4096 input tokens, 1/256 output tokens, concurrency 1/8/64 and staggered arrivals. Adaptive and TP=2 runs include varied chat/code prompts.

<details>
<summary>Commands and output comparison</summary>

```bash
uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd_cug.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_mode.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_dispatch.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py -q

uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py
```

Initial validation had three GPU memory-profiling failures across baseline/candidate; all passed after isolation. The follow-up rerun passed all 87 tests without retries.

Greedy tokens matched for 1,022 requests / 123,382 output tokens against baseline runs/repeats. Initial asynchronous differences on 1 adaptive and 4 TP=2 requests also occurred in unmodified-upstream A/A runs; those repeats matched the candidate. This is not a claim of bitwise reproducibility or a speedup.

</details>

## Details

Decode planning retains speculative-length expansion, variable-length handling, rounding and deduplication; mixed planning retains its request-shape constraints. `FULL` keeps its mixed-routine semantics. Runtime dispatch and graph capture are unchanged.
Retains `defaultdict(list)` for descriptor aggregation, preserving the import needed when composed with #56136.

No duplicate refactor found in issue/PR searches. Related #56136 changes candidate ladders, #60265 changes the default capture ceiling, and #60989 adds standalone-draft graph support; this PR changes none of those policies.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

nodes.body:
@SouthWest7 — I author #56136, which rewrites the candidate-ladder tail of the same
function, so I checked whether the two changes compose. They merge cleanly and the composed
function does not run.

Revisions checked:

- #61882 head: `8fbd91d17a2c36674aec38cb963bb6bb3638aa31`
- #56136 head: `6ab4d6a43f774da091d5d3884c68674ae8d7b9fe`
- merge base: `7d1d8660d620149bc4eadf795cbb80a1f884ddc2`

A 3-way merge of `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py` at those three revisions completes
with **no conflicts** — the two hunks are adjacent but do not overlap.

This refactor removes `from collections import defaultdict`, correctly, since
`descs_by_mode` becomes a plain `dict`. #56136 adds a `defaultdict(list)` in the ladder loop,
using the import that is present on the merge base, so the composed file contains that call
with no binding for it. Extracting the composed `_init_candidates` and running it against a
minimal stub object:

```
composed file as-is               ->  NameError: name 'defaultdict' is not defined
                                      (raised inside _init_candidates)
same run, `defaultdict` supplied  ->  completes: 33 candidate keys, 4 FULL descriptors
```

Supplying that one name is the only difference between the two runs.

Neither PR is merged, so none of this describes current `main`, and I did not start an
engine, build vLLM, or run anything on a GPU. The point is only that if these two land
together, the import needs to stay.

Thanks for checking this. I reproduced the clean-merge `NameError` against #56136 at `6ab4d6a43f`.

Fixed in ff53d80dde by retaining `defaultdict(list)` for descriptor aggregation, so the import remains used. Both three-way merge orders now produce the same conflict-free file; all 46 combined planner/dynamic-SD tests pass, including your strided-ladder regression.

Also reran the 87-test suite, pre-commit, and 960 configurations / 76,800 dispatch comparisons. Qwen3-4B/DFlash MRV2 smoke passed with dynamic K=5/3/1, actual FULL graph replay and nonzero acceptance.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.
